plan: Model all patient-facing state as the public `session` dictionary with exactly the four contract keys, produced by a single `_initial_session()` factory used for construction, begin, and abandon resets.
Copy the appointment sequence (id/label dicts) at construction and keep an id set for O(1) validation, rebuilding fresh choice dictionaries per screen in input order.
Dispatch `handle` through a class-level table mapping action type strings to handler methods; unknown types, non-dict actions, and bad payloads short-circuit to an error screen.
Have every handler validate preconditions (active/incomplete session, boolean flags, known appointment ids) before any mutation so rejected actions leave accepted data untouched and never raise.

Derive prompts from post-action state via `_next_prompt` (Confirm contact -> Choose appointment -> Review and complete), reused for corrections and for error screens over unchanged state; special-case completion and abandon prompts/messages.
Centralize screen construction in `_screen`, which enforces the exact prompt/messages/choices shape and includes appointment choices only when the prompt is `Choose appointment`.

Implement `run_once` with injected `action_source`/`screen_sink` collaborators: raise RuntimeError before any call if either is missing, otherwise read one action, handle it, display the screen once, and return that same object, enabling standard-library unittest fakes.
mechanisms: Action-type dispatch table (`_HANDLERS`) mapping frozen action names to handler methods
Validate-then-mutate handler discipline guaranteeing no state corruption on rejected actions
Single `_initial_session()` factory for initial state, clean begin, and abandon reset
State-derived prompt resolution (`_next_prompt`/`_current_prompt`) yielding the next unmet step
Centralized `_screen` builder enforcing the exact screen shape and choices-only-on-appointment-prompt rule
Defensive copying of appointments plus an id membership set for input validation
Constructor-injected `action_source`/`screen_sink` ports with a RuntimeError guard in `run_once` for fake-based testing
